title: Wait for the Liquidity Grab
spoken_transcript:
Kind: captions
Language: en
Every time price does this, you should
not be entering a trade.
What you're looking at here is a classic
liquidity grab. See these equal highs?
Every single retail trader who went
short placed their stop loss right above
them.
In smart money concepts, we call this
buy-side liquidity. It's not a
resistance level. It's a pool of orders
that institutions need to fill their
positions. So, what does price do? It
pushes up, breaks above those highs,
triggers all those stop losses, and then
immediately reverses.
That move upward was not a breakout.
That was a hunt. After liquidity is
taken, smart money has what it needs.
The orders are filled. Now, price can
move in the real direction. This is why
you kept getting stopped out trading
breakouts. You were the liquidity. Once
you understand this, you stop chasing
breakouts. You start waiting for the
sweep. You let price take the liquidity,
then you look for your entry in the
opposite direction.
